title: Explicit internal group action site and coefficient sheaf, independent of presentation
statement: Let C be a small category and K:C^op -> Grp a group presheaf in the same universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Define C_K to have objects Object(K) with a base object of C, arrows (f,a):X -> Y with f:X.base -> Y.base and a in K(X.base), identity (id,1), and composition (f,a) followed by (g,b) equal to (f followed by g, a * K(f)(b)). Projection forgets a. For a precoverage J on C [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], a presieve R covers in C_K exactly when its image {f | there exists a, (f,a) in R} covers in J. Equip C_K with the generated Grothendieck topology. The base sieve of a twisted sieve consists of its label-one arrows; a twisted sieve covers exactly when this base sieve covers in J.toGrothendieck. If C has finite limits and J is a site for coverings, singleton isomorphisms cover and covers admit covering pullbacks, with lifted legs (p,1) and (q,K(p)(a) * K(q)(b)^(-1)). For a commutative ring sheaf S, define the coefficient presheaf by projection followed by S; this is a sheaf. Define its underlying ring sheaf by forgetting commutativity. Equivariant categories and their forgetful functors are the existing definitions [def-sfb-internal-equivariant-module-sheaves], re-exported without alteration.

proof.text: Construct objects and arrows as structures and composition by the displayed formula. The group homomorphism and functor identities prove the category laws. Base pullback universality determines the unique base lift; its label is forced by the first leg, and the cone equation gives the second leg. Project isomorphism covers and use the base covering-pullback axiom. Reuse the existing sieve-geometry arrow_ext and labeled_pullback proofs, relocated here as shared public lemmas so both covering_pullbacks and sieve_geometry use one construction.

Sieve membership is independent of the label by precomposition with (id,a) and (id,a inverse). Taking all labels over a base sieve inverts taking label-one arrows, and commutes with pullbacks and generated sieves. Transport topologies in both directions along these inverse operations. Induction over the generated topology in both directions proves the covering characterization, including the empty presieve.

For a matching family of the coefficient presheaf on a twisted covering sieve, retain its label-one members, glue in S, and use compatibility with vertical arrows to check all other members and uniqueness. Applying this to each coyoneda test object proves the commutative-ring sheaf condition. The remaining action-category laws follow by linearity, componentwise composition, and subtype extensionality.
